conventions.convention: Couplings are countably additive probabilities on the full Borel sigma-algebra of the product topology; equality with the sigma-algebra generated by Borel rectangles is not assumed.
The transport cost is an extended-real infimum, with infimum of the empty coupling set equal to +∞.
Nearest-center quantization uses distinct ordered centers, assigns ties to the least index, and has displacement strictly less than the positive scale.
The dual objective is integral against μ minus integral against ν, with real 1-Lipschitz tests normalized by f(x₀)=0.
Countable Choice is assumed explicitly for the second-countability reduction; the general compact-space theorem instead uses section products and does not select a sequence of nets or plans.
The compact-space equality asserts neither primal nor dual attainment; finite-scale primal and dual attainment are separate supplier results.

load_bearing.statement: For nonempty compact metric spaces X,Y and countably additive Borel probabilities μ,ν, every product-topology Borel set E has Borel sections and a Borel section-measure function x ↦ ν(E_x). The formula λ(E)=∫ν(E_x)dμ defines a Borel probability with λ(A×B)=μ(A)ν(B) for Borel A,B.

For a compact or second-countable metric space, a finite Borel partition with centers at displacement less than ε, Borel probabilities μ,ν, and a finite coupling π of the cell masses, there is a Borel coupling γ of μ,ν with ∫d(x,y)dγ ≤ Σᵢⱼπᵢⱼd(xᵢ,xⱼ)+2ε.

Every nonempty compact metric space and ε>0 admit distinct ordered centers, a Borel nearest-center partition with least-index tie breaking, and a Borel quantization map Q satisfying d(x,Q(x))<ε everywhere.
For a finite nonempty ordered subset of a metric space and values satisfying |fᵢ−fⱼ|≤d(xᵢ,xⱼ), the function minᵢ(fᵢ+d(x,xᵢ)) is 1-Lipschitz and equals fᵢ at each xᵢ.

On a nonempty compact metric space, for countably additive Borel probabilities μ,ν and a fixed x₀, the Borel coupling set is nonempty and W₁ˣ(μ,ν)=sup{∫f dμ−∫f dν : f:X→ℝ, f(x₀)=0, |f(x)−f(y)|≤d(x,y) for all x,y}.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If (X,d) is a compact metric space, then its metric topology has an at-most-countable basis; equivalently, X is second-countable.

seams_checked.note: Both compact duality proofs use the finite theorem for a nonempty finite metric space, probability-vector marginals, first-coordinate normalization, equality of primal and signed dual values, and finite attainment. The finite supplier states all these conclusions, including singleton and zero-coordinate cases.

The WGAN theorem's F2 and Proof 1.2 use the compact theorem with Borel probabilities and anchored Lipschitz tests. Symmetry under negation justifies the absolute IPM formulation. Critic attainment is separately assumed for the gradient formula; no attainment conclusion is imported from compact duality.

The page declares this prerequisite, but its listed items contain no citation to the compact KR items. The inspected transport arguments instead prove squared-Euclidean-cost optimality using a separate affine-dilation lemma; they do not apply compact W₁ duality to noncompact Gaussian laws.
